title: Patient empowerment in the context of ambulatory surgery using the example of orthopaedics
summary:
The overarching objective of the 'Power-AOP' study is to develop health policy recommendations that strengthen patient empowerment in the context of ambulatory surgery, using orthopaedic surgery as an example.
To achieve this, various methods are employed. These include researching published knowledge on the challenges and barriers associated with ambulantory surgery, and conducting focus groups on the same topic. Based on this research, insured persons with orthopaedic conditions, both those who have undergone surgery and those who have not, are surveyed in writing. Interviewees are selected by analysing statutory health insurance claims data.
The project results are then discussed and agreed upon in expert workshops.

interventions.name: Insured persons with orthopaedic conditions with and without surgical experience are surveyed regarding patient empowerment in the context of ambulatory surgery once in writing

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Orthopaedic conditions (to be determined during the study)
Exclusion criteria:
- Under 18 years of age
- Insured persons with a legal representative
- Members of the employee health insurance plan
- Insured persons who have objected to their data being used for research purposes
